I was told not to use tools, so I can't write `update.md` or read the full files. Below is the content to paste into `update.md`. I only saw the lines you quoted, so each section gives those lines rather than full files. Everything else in each file stays the same.

**One pushback:** you asked for "no cleverness, fastest path only," but retry logic and logging changes are new behavior I can't test against code I haven't seen. That's the kind of change that breaks a demo. I've put them in a separate optional section so you can ship the URL fix now and add the rest after the demo.

---

```markdown
# update.md

## scripts/fetch_users.py

Change:
    BASE = "https://api.oldhost.com/v2"
To:
    BASE = "https://api.newhost.io/v2"

(`requests.get(BASE + "/users")` is unchanged and now hits the new host.)

## scripts/fetch_orders.py

Change:
    url = "https://api.oldhost.com/v2/orders"
To:
    url = "https://api.newhost.io/v2/orders"

## README

Change:
    All data comes from https://api.oldhost.com/v2
To:
    All data comes from https://api.newhost.io/v2

## Notes

- Only the three quoted lines were visible, so this is a line-level diff, not full file
  contents. All other lines are unchanged.
- Before the demo, grep for stragglers: `grep -rn "oldhost" .`
  (env files, configs, tests, and CI could also hold the old URL.)
- Retry logic and logging improvements are deliberately NOT applied. See the optional
  section below. They're new behavior and untested, so applying them after the demo is safer.

## Optional (post-demo): retry + logging

Add near the top of each script:

    import logging
    import requests
    from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
    from urllib3.util.retry import Retry

    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

    session = requests.Session()
    session.mount("https://", HTTPAdapter(max_retries=Retry(
        total=3, backoff_factor=0.5,
        status_forcelist=(429, 500, 502, 503, 504),
        allowed_methods=("GET",),
    )))

Then replace the call, e.g. in fetch_orders.py:

    log.info("GET %s", url)
    resp = session.get(url, timeout=10)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    log.info("GET %s -> %s", url, resp.status_code)

(Same pattern in fetch_users.py with `BASE + "/users"`.)

Note: `raise_for_status()` and `timeout=10` change behavior. Failures will now raise
instead of continuing silently, so check how the rest of each script handles the response.
```
